authoredNote: Lines read off `nl -ba` of this file: imports 9-11 (external item, namespace, relative item), externalHelper.run() 20, ns.readFileSync 21, localThing.run 25, d.run 29. The claim marker is an OBJECT (not pinnable by reference); the analyzer publishes scalar mirrors for fixtures and the object for the arbiter: `meta.importedBindingSpecifier` / `meta.importedBindingName`, plus the imports-edge evidence as an ARRAY (`meta.importedBindings`).
rationale: PINS THE IMPORTED-BINDING CLAIM IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Positive: a call through a binding imported from an EXTERNAL package (`externalHelper.run()`) and through a NAMESPACE binding of a node builtin (`ns.readFileSync`) carry `metadata.importedBinding` with the specifier and the receiver-root binding — the rows the name model cannot resolve and the index-side external claims cannot reach (namespace imports and shadowed packages have no `module:item` spelling to claim from). The imports edges publish the evidence the arbiter verifies against: `meta.importedBindings` (array of local names) with `meta.module` (the specifier as written). Negative A: `localThing` is imported from a RELATIVE module — project-local, so the claim is withheld (claiming it would launder a resolvable edge as a binding). Negative B: `d.run()` has a receiver whose type the file declares — not an imported binding, so no marker. This pair is what makes the claim falsifiable from both sides. RE-EXPORT EXCLUSION (2026-10-19, whole-population defect round): an export-from edge is a module dependency whose item is the name asked for, not a local binding — the first emission was publishing it as import evidence and could fabricate claims from a barrel file. The edge carries `metadata.isReExport: true` and NO `importedBindings`, pinned positive+forbid.
